data.description:
## Context
The narrow rich-emission operation exists after S2, but production still mutates a binding reached through `all_bindings()`. ADR 0099 also needs the realized recovery boundary and reversal rules. `apply_handlers.py` overlaps RP-04 S3 and must be rebased after that ticket lands.

## Outcome
Route production rich-emission state through the authoritative facade, remove production mutation-through-query, and finalize ADR 0099 without changing output, storage, or tickets publication.

## Plan
1. Before implementation, confirm RP-04 S3 `talismanic-profitable-isopod` is closed and rebase on its landed `apply_handlers.py`; do not edit the RP-04 ticket.
2. Replace only the rich-emission inner-dict mutation with the S2 facade operation. Preserve hashes, counters, missing-binding behavior, logs, and baseline effects.
3. Add a production-code census/poison test that fails when binding mutation is reached through `all_bindings()`.
4. Finalize ADR 0099 with tombstone authority, explicit-unretire reversal, pre-observation recovery, intentional delta, rollback, and the ban on broad tickets-branch staging.

## Testing
Run rich-reemit, apply-handler, recovery-boundary, and ADR index suites against the RP-04-integrated base.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] RP-04 S3 is closed and its landed `apply_handlers.py` is the implementation base.
- [ ] Production rich-emission behavior uses the narrow facade operation and preserves existing hashes, counters, logs, and missing-binding outcomes.
- [ ] No production code mutates a binding through `all_bindings()`.
- [ ] Binding/event file bytes and selective publication remain unchanged outside the approved repair.
- [ ] ADR 0099 records the realized repair, ordering, explicit reversal, rollback, and no-broad-staging decision.

## Out of scope
Configuration/secrets changes remain owned by RP-04.
data.title: RP-02 S3 T3 — Cut rich-emission writes to the facade and finalize ADR 0099
